briefdescription.para: Specify a proxy to use (optionally may be prefixed with a scheme - e.g.

detaileddescription.para: If this option is not set a value from the corresponding environment variable will be used. Environment variable names are: 'http_proxy', 'https_proxy', 'ftp_proxy' etc. 'all_proxy' variable is used if no protocol specific proxy was set.
Setting this option to an empty string will explicitly disable the use of a proxy, even if there is an environment variable set for it.

parameterdescription.para: - a host name or an IP address. The application does not have to keep the string around after setting this option.

briefdescription.para: Specify a comma separated list of host names that do not require a proxy to get reached, even if one is specified by 'proxy' option.

detaileddescription.para: The only wildcard available is a single * character, which matches all hosts, and effectively disables the proxy.
'no_proxy' environment variable will be used if this option is not set.
Setting this option to an empty string will explicitly enable the proxy for all host names, even if there is an environment variable set for it.

parameterdescription.para: - a comma separated list of host names. The application does not have to keep the string around after setting this option.

Enable automatic decompression of HTTP responses: set the contents of the Accept-Encoding header sent in a HTTP request and enable decoding of a response when a Content-Encoding header is received.

detaileddescription.para: This is a request, not an order; the server may or may not do it. Servers might respond with Content-Encoding even without getting an Accept-Encoding in the request. Servers might respond with a different Content-Encoding than what was asked for in the request.

req
request
encoding
- specify what encoding you'd like. This param can be an empty string which means Accept-Encoding header will contain all built-in supported encodings. This param can be comma-separated list of accepted encodings, like: "br, gzip, deflate".
Bundled libcurl supports "identity", meaning non-compressed, "deflate" which requests the server to compress its response using the zlib algorithm and "gzip" which requests the gzip algorithm. System libcurl also possibly supports "br" which is brotli.
